Subject: Renewal + uplift questions — Private Offer routing and SLA carryover

Sergio,

Thanks for the call last week. We ran an internal usage forecast (attached) and expect a ~2.3x uplift for H2. Procurement is ready to move to a private offer, but we have two constraints: 1) our PO process requires a staggered acceptance for FY tranching, and 2) our security/compliance team needs confirmation that the SLA and uptime commitments in the current contract carry forward to the new private-offer arrangement.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept two linked POs (signed at different dates) that map to the same private-offer commitment and whether SLA obligations will remain intact across the stagger? If there are any evidence buckets we should be preparing (audit logs, SOC2 attestations, KMS attestations), please list them so we can get procurement and security aligned.

We'd like to close by end of month if terms and routing look straightforward. Attach: HeliosPay_Projected_Usage_Q3Q4.xlsx

Regards,
Elaine Carter
CFO | HeliosPay

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift questions — Private Offer routing and SLA carryover

Thanks Elaine — appreciate the file and the clarity. Short answers up front: yes, we can support multiple linked POs as tranche acceptance (we call it "staggered acceptance") and yes, SLA obligations can carry across to the private-offer if the acceptance criteria are met at each tranche event.

Notes / immediate asks: 
- Can your procurement team confirm the exact tranche dates and PO numbering convention? We need distinct PO identifiers to map invoices.
- We will prepare an "evidence bundle" for the security gate: SOC2 Type II report (current), configuration snapshot (KMS provider type + key rotation window), and sample audit logs for a month. Priyom, can you confirm the exact evidence filenames we typically deliver for marketplace private-offer acceptance?

Proposed operational plan:
1) Sign PO-1 (covers initial commit + immediate onboarding) — DocuSign link from our side.
2) Sign PO-2 (remaining capacity) within the agreed tranche window (we support up to 90 days between POs).
3) At each acceptance event, our billing will emit an invoice linked to the corresponding PO. SLA remains active once the first PO acceptance criteria are satisfied; subsequent POs increase committed capacity and do not reset SLA start.

I'll loop Kimberly for invoice routing and Jordan for any marketplace/legal flow that requires the cloud marketplace private-offer object.

— Sergio Alvarez
Head of Marketplace Deals | Redwood Inference
